storm.summary_layperson: No storms anywhere nearby tonight. It's a dry, chilly evening with a brisk north wind behind this morning's cold front.
storm.local_effect_blurb: The Sound (65°F) is about 17°F warmer than the air at 4 PM, and the gap widens to roughly 25°F by 8 PM as the air cools. That means there is no cool marine layer to shelter the cove at any point tonight, but with no storms around it doesn't matter.
storm.detail_html:
Regional picture: KOKX radar shows no echoes to track. There are no NWS watches, warnings or advisories, and the atmosphere has no storm fuel at all (CAPE 0 J/kg in the latest HRRR run and the NWS discussion). Air pressure is high and steady around 1023 hPa, and a dry northerly flow covers the whole region from the Hudson Valley to Block Island.

Local modifier: On summer afternoons the Sound is colder than the air, and that cool layer over the water often weakens storms before they reach the cove. Tonight it's the other way round. The water is 65°F and the air is about 48°F, so the Sound is roughly 17°F warmer. The Sound holds its temperature while the air keeps cooling after sunset (6:10 PM), so the gap grows to about 25°F by 8 PM. No protective layer exists at any point in the evening, and there's nothing for one to protect against.

Cove vs. surroundings: Expect the same dry weather in Greenwich as inland Westchester and along the rest of the Connecticut shore. The one local difference is wind: the warm water stirs up the air just above it, so gusts on the water will stay sharper than on land after dark.

What would change the call: Nothing in the data points to storms. This stays low unless new radar returns appear to the west, which is very unlikely in this cold, dry air.

wind.regime_label: Moderate north wind from the weather system – no sea breeze

hourly.shift_note: easing slightly at sunset, still shifty
steady, puffs from the NW shore

wind.tactics_blurb: A cold northerly blowing off the land: puffy and shifty, with big swings in direction. Stay near the middle of the course and tack on the 15–20° headers rather than banking on one side.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
Regime: This is a moderate gradient-wind day, meaning the wind comes from the large-scale weather pattern and there's no sea breeze. A sea breeze needs the land to be warmer than the water. Today the air (about 48°F inland) is roughly 17°F colder than the Sound (65°F), and none of the 18 coastal stations show any southerly flow. The regional wind is a solid north breeze behind the cold front. Airports and other well-sited stations average 10.9 kt, the NWS forecast calls for north at around 20 mph this afternoon, and Riverside YC is reading N 9.6 kt (10-minute average 10.9 kt, gusting 18.8). Because the wind isn't driven by the sun, it won't shut off at sunset (6:10 PM). Expect it to ease 2–3 kt after dark and keep blowing from the north.

Direction: The HRRR model shows NNW (331–348°), but stations around the western Sound and the club anemometer read due north (359° and 9°). That's a 28° gap, so we're using the observed north as the baseline instead of the model. This is a gradient-wind day, not a sea-breeze day, so the sea-breeze direction correction does not apply.

Where the pressure is: A north wind blows off the land, so it reaches the cove over trees and houses. That makes it puffy and gusty, with direction swings of 15–20° or more. In this direction the most reliable pressure is usually in the middle of the cove, away from the wind shadow close to either shore. Big puffs come off the northwest shore with lighter holes in between. Nearby stations confirm the effect: inland stations just upwind are almost calm (1–5 kt), while Riverside YC and Old Greenwich read about 10 kt. The breeze is coming down from above and hitting the water in bursts.

Through the evening: Expect 10–11 kt at 5 PM with gusts in the high teens, easing to about 8 kt by 7 PM and 7 kt by 10 PM. The Sound is much warmer than the air, which keeps the air over the water mixing, so the breeze on the water should hold up better after dark than it does on land. Gust-to-lull swings stay large all evening. Sail the shifts: tack on the headers and keep your head out of the boat to spot dark patches coming off the shore.

What it feels like: Comfortable full-crew breeze early, then lighter-air trim after sunset. It will be cold: around 51°F now and falling into the low 40s by 8 PM, and the north wind makes it feel colder. Dress for it.

data_caveats: The latest HRRR model run (19Z) only covered up to 8 PM. The 9–10 PM numbers are extended from the 7–8 PM trend, so they're less certain.
The HRRR model doesn't give gust values. Gusts are estimated from the gust-to-average ratio at Riverside YC.
HRRR (NNW 331°) differs from the observed wind (due N) by 28°. Forecast directions use the observed north as the baseline.
HRRR wind speeds are running about 3 kt lighter than what Riverside YC is measuring, so forecast speeds are anchored to the club's anemometer.
